correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the transform in interface-centered coordinates. For k=sqrt(s/D), boundedness on the right gives u'(b+)=-k u(b+), and continuity of flux and the backward jump law give u'(b-)=-k u(b+) and u(b-)=(1+Dk/kappa)u(b+). Propagating the left solution back to 0 gives 1=u(b+)[(1+Dk/kappa)cosh(kb)+sinh(kb)]. Propagating right to L and simplifying gives exactly the stated Laplace transform. Under global resets, each independent trial has success probability phi(r)>0 and mean duration (1-phi(r))/r, yielding the normalized F after renewal. For convexity, write the transparent term as integral_0^1 e^(u z)/z du; the second derivative of each e^(a z)/z is e^(a z)[(a z-1)^2+1]/z^3, positive for all real a. This also applies to the two resistance terms. Both endpoint limits are infinity, so the stationary root is unique and interior. Differentiation gives F_B=-2 eta exp((1-2B)z) and F_zB=(1-2B)F_B; implicit differentiation and the positive curvature give the exact signed slope, while the envelope derivative gives strict decrease of the minimized mean. The monotone rate conversion preserves the unique maximum exactly at B=1/2. The proof requires finite positive permeability and resets from both sides as claimed. The recorded finite sweep was not rerun and is not used to establish the universal quantifier.
